"NFL season" redirects here. For a list of all seasons, see List of NFL seasons .

The National Football League (NFL) regular season begins on the weekend following the first Monday of September (i.e., the weekend following the Labor Day") holiday) and ends in early January, after which that season's playoffs tournament begins. It consists of 272 games, with each of the NFL's 32 teams playing 17 games during an 18-week period with one " bye") " week off.

Since 2012, the NFL generally schedules games in five time slots during the week. The first game of the week is played on Thursday night , kicking off at 8:15 pm ET except for the kickoff game and Thanksgiving games, which kick off at 8:20 pm. The majority of games are played on Sunday, most kicking off at 1 pm ET, with some late afternoon games starting at either 4:05 or 4:25 pm ET. Additionally, one Sunday night game is played every week at 8:20 pm ET.

In its early years after 1920 , the NFL did not have a set schedule, and teams played as few as one and as many as sixteen games, many against independent professional, college, or amateur teams. From 1926 through 1946 , they played from eleven to fourteen games per season, depending on the number of teams in the league. From 1947 through 1960 , each NFL team played 12 games per season.

...

A seventeenth regular season game was added in 2021 . [[ 7 ]](:0-8)

Since the 2002 season, the league has scheduled a nationally televised regular season NFL Kickoff Game on the Thursday night after Labor Day, prior to the first Sunday of NFL games to kick off the season. The first one, featuring the San Francisco 49ers and the New York Giants , was held on September 5, 2002, largely to celebrate New York City's resilience in the wake of the September 11, 2001 attacks . [[ 8 ]]() Since 2004, the NFL has indicated that the opening game will normally be hosted by the defending Super Bowl champions as the official start of their title defense. Under this scheduling system, the earliest the regular season could begin is September 4, as it was in the 2008 , 2014 , and 2025 seasons, due to September 1 falling on a Monday, while the latest possible is September 10, as it was in the 2009 , 2015 , and 2020 seasons, and will be in the 2026 season, due to September 1 falling on a Tuesday.

...

Between 1970 and the 2002 expansion to 32 teams, the league used scheduling rubrics with similarities to the present model, though they were adjusted for the number of teams and divisions.

The only time between the merger and 2002 (when the league was realigned into eight divisions of four teams each) that the league was completely "balanced" was in 1995 to 1998 (with six divisions of five teams each). When the league did not have equal numbers of teams in every division, every team's opposition could not be determined by the same means.

While teams playing against their division rivals twice each has been a tradition since 1933 , when divisions were first introduced (the first standardized schedule), not all teams would play the same number of divisional games due to the imbalances noted in the preceding paragraph.

...

During these years, teams in five-team divisions who did not finish last would not face any fifth-place team outside their division, whether or not those teams were intraconference.

This scheduling system meant that, apart from the AFC Central and NFC West, all of whose teams would regularly meet every three years, teams would not necessarily play teams outside their division on a regular basis, although teams who never finished fifth would play teams in the other conference who likewise avoided last position on the same three-season cycle.

The 1987 strike and subsequent lockout") lasted 24 days but only one week of the schedule was lost. Weeks 4 through 6 were played with non-union replacement players . The rest of the season was played as originally scheduled, for a total of 15 games per team.

In the event that the 2011 season had been disrupted because of a then-ongoing labor dispute, the NFL had arranged its schedule to facilitate easier cancellations and postponements. In addition to an emergency scenario of an eight-game schedule beginning in late November, the NFL also arranged its full-length schedule such that weeks 2 and 4 had no division games and all week 3 matchups could be moved into each team's respective bye week.

The 2026 NFL season won't start until the Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots on Sept. 9 in a Super Bowl 60 rematch. However, football fans won't have to wait that long to see their favorite teams take the field.

The NFL preseason will begin on Thursday, Aug. 6 when the Arizona Cardinals face the Carolina Panthers at the league's annual Hall of Fame game in Canton, Ohio. An addition 48 games will be played over the following weeks, with each of the league's 32 participating in at least three exhibition contests.

In recent seasons, NFL teams have been less and less willing to give their starters extensive playing time in the preseason. Even so, football fans are always eager to see how their favorite squad's recent draft picks and roster hopefuls perform, especially mid-to-late-round quarterbacks who are looking to prove they can be NFL contributors.
Among the top signal-callers to watch during the 2026 preseason will be first-round quarterbacks Fernando Mendoza and Ty Simpson, Day 2 signal-callers Carson Beck and Drew Allar and New York Jets fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik.

Here's a full look at the NFL's preseason schedule for 2026 and when fans can see their favorite teams in action before the season begins in earnest.

2026 NFL preseason schedule

The NFC, meanwhile, will be a highly contested conference with many teams that believe they have a chance to make a run to the Super Bowl in Los Angeles this season.

Here's a look at when the 2026 NFL season will begin.

**NFL HQ:** [Live NFL scores](https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/scores) | [Updated NFL standings](https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/standings) | [Full NFL schedule](https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/schedule)

## When does the NFL season start in 2026?

* **Date** : Wednesday, Sept. 9
* **Game** : Patriots at Seahawks
* **Kickoff time** : 8:20 p.m. ET

The NFL season typically opens on a Thursday, but this year the season begins on the Wednesday after Labor Day. The reason for this is because there is another Thursday game, which is taking place in Australia on September 10.

As always, the defending Super Bowl champion will host the first game of the year, with the Seahawks raising their second banner.
They will be doing so in a Super Bowl rematch, as the [New England Patriots](https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/new-england-patriots) will hope to get revenge after losing to Seattle in February.

This marks the third time in NFL history that a Super Bowl rematch will open the season and the first time since 2016. It is also the second time the Seahawks have hosted an opening game, as they defeated the [Green Bay Packers](https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/green-bay-packers) in 2014 to kick off their first defending championship season.

With Labor Day falling on the latest possible date, the NFL season begins as late as it could be. The first Sunday of the NFL season is on September 13, almost halfway through the month of September.

## NFL Schedule Week 1

Week 1 in the 2026 NFL season will feature 16 games across four days.

### Key Takeaways

* The 2026 NFL preseason begins with the Hall of Fame Game on August 6 in Canton, Ohio, featuring the Carolina Panthers vs. the Arizona Cardinals on NBC and Peacock.
* Preseason Week 1 games take place August 13–15, followed by Week 2 starting August 20 and Week 3 concluding August 27–29.
* The 2026–2027 NFL regular season officially starts on September 9 with a _Sunday Night Football_ kickoff game between the Seahawks and Patriots on NBC and Peacock.

It's only the beginning of July, but summer will be over before you know it. While that's sad news in many ways, it also means something quite joyous: Football season is on the way!

## How to Watch
Watch _Sunday Night Football_ on [NBC](https://www.nbc.com/sports/league/nfl) and streaming on [Peacock](https://www.peacocktv.com/sports/nfl?cid=2411evginsdredinbcrownedi26430&utm_campaign=2411evginsdredi&utm_source=insdredi_nbcupt_st-sv&utm_medium=own_edi_awa_artl&utm_term=insidereditorialreaders&utm_content=sundaynightfootball2025) .

In the coming weeks, [NFL](https://www.peacocktv.com/sports/nfl?cid=2411evginsdredinbcrownedi26430&utm_campaign=2411evginsdredi&utm_source=insdredi_nbcupt_st-sv&utm_medium=own_edi_awa_artl&utm_term=insidereditorialreaders&utm_content=sundaynightfootball2025) teams will begin assembling their training camps for rookies, key position players, and more, gearing up for the arrival of preseason football and, soon after, the launch of [the 2026-2027 NFL regular season](https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/the-full-2026-2027-nfl-schedule) . That means the return of [_Sunday Night Football_](https://www.nbc.
com/nbc-insider/show/sunday-night-football) on **NBC** and [Peacock](https://www.peacocktv.com/sports/nfl?cid=2411evginsdredinbcrownedi27418&utm_campaign=2411evginsdredi&utm_source=insdredi_nbcupt_st-sv&utm_medium=own_edi_awa_artl&utm_term=insidereditorialreaders&utm_content=nfl) , but before that can happen, we've got to get the preseason games going.

So, when does the preseason actually start? Let's take a look at some key dates.

**RELATED:** [**Here's When** _**Sunday Night Football**_ **Returns to NBC**](https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/heres-when-sunday-night-football-2026-kicks-off)

The [NFL Draft](https://www.nbc.com/nbc-insider/nfl-draft-order-2026-revealed-who-has-the-no-1-pick-in-the-draft) is over, and July is the time for teams across the league to begin their respective training camps, beginning with camp for rookies and eventually expanding to include the entire roster.
Teams will have most of July to get their rosters together, begin camps, and sign free agents before the start of preseason play in August.

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes out on the field with his teammates during Day 2 of minicamp practice.

Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, #15, out on the field with his teammates during Day 2 of minicamp practice in Kansas City, Missouri, on June 10, 2026. Photo: Emily Curiel/The Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service/Getty Images

## When does the NFL preseason begin in 2026?

As always, the preseason will be inaugurated by the 2026 NFL Hall of Fame Game, honoring the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame class and officially kicking off exhibition matchups. This year's NFL Hall of Fame Game is set for August 6, live on **NBC** and [Peacock](https://www.peacocktv.com/sports/nfl?
cid=2411evginsdredinbcrownedi26430&utm_campaign=2411evginsdredi&utm_source=insdredi_nbcupt_st-sv&utm_medium=own_edi_awa_artl&utm_term=insidereditorialreaders&utm_content=sundaynightfootball2025) , from Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton, Ohio, featuring the Carolina Panthers vs. the Arizona Cardinals.

Week 1 of the preseason officially kicks off one week later, with games airing on August 13, 14, and 15. Week 2 follows beginning August 20, and Week 3 concludes the preseason with games on August 27, 28, and 29.

## When does the NFL regular season begin?

Keep an eye on _**NBC Insider**_ for the latest info on the schedule and how to watch the biggest NFL games on **NBC** and Peacock all season-long.
